slides.title: Sixteen Transitions. One Prompt. No Margin.
slides.subtitle: The status matrix is where imprecise prompts result in multi-week remediation

hero_stat.label: valid transitions across 6 states — every transition must be specified in the prompt or AI will invent incorrect rules

analogy.title: Chess versus draughts
analogy.text: Draughts permits informal specification. Chess does not — castling, en passant, promotion all require explicit rules before play commences. Status workflows operate at chess complexity; ad hoc specification produces incorrect outputs.

bullets: Six states — Open, InProgress, InReview, Resolved, Closed, Reopened.
Thirteen valid transitions, two explicitly prohibited transitions, and one same-status-comment pattern — sixteen total.
Omission of any element produces transitions AI invents — breaking the audit trail.
Quantified cost — two to three days of remediation after launch when QA identifies the defects.

slides.title: Why Workflows Are AI's Most Challenging Domain
slides.subtitle: Four causes — each one a failure mode if unaddressed

list.name: Domain-specific rules
list.desc: No standardised workflow exists. The organisation's workflow is unique. AI has no training data for it. Without explicit specification, AI fabricates plausible alternatives.

list.name: State combinatorial expansion
list.desc: Six states permit thirty possible transitions (6 × 5). Most must be prohibited. AI defaults to permissive behaviour unless prohibitions are stated explicitly.

list.name: Side-effects per transition
list.desc: Each transition may trigger emails, audit log entries, or field locking. AI omits side-effects unless explicitly required. Omitted side-effects produce silent defects.

list.name: UI–API parity
list.desc: The dropdown must display only permitted next states. The API must enforce the identical matrix. AI commonly implements one and omits the other. UI is not enforcement.

slides.closing_thread: All four are addressed by a single structured prompt.

slides.title: The Marker Pillar — In Practice
slides.subtitle: From Module 3 — the practical realisation of P.R.O.M.P.T.'s M
bullets: Marker — the boundaries within which AI may operate.

slides.title: Day 5 — The Collaboration Layer
slides.subtitle: Comments and attachments — the audit-bearing spine of every issue tracker
bullets: Comments are not merely textual content — they constitute the audit trail of issue progression.
Each comment is associated with the status active at the time of posting. Some comments effect status transitions; both are first-class events.
Attachments introduce additional concerns — file size constraints, MIME-type allow-listing, virus scanning hooks, signed URLs.
Either omission produces — at minimum — a compromised audit trail; at worst, an XSS or RCE vector via the upload pipeline.

slides.subtitle: Status dropdown · mandatory comment · resolution and reason requirements

bullets: Status dropdown — displays CURRENT status plus PERMITTED next statuses only, per the matrix. No 'no-change' option permitted.
Posting with current status — comment saved; no transition record. Audit log records a comment event only.
Posting with new status — comment saved; transition record written; side-effects executed (emails, notifications).
Resolved — requires resolution note in a separate field. Reopened — requires reason in a separate field. Both server-validated.
Attachments on comment — maximum five files per comment, ten megabytes each, MIME allow-list (pdf, png, jpg, txt, docx). Server-validated.

slides.title: File Upload Security — Safe Versus Unsafe Patterns
slides.subtitle: AI defaults to UNSAFE unless boundaries are explicitly defined

table.orch: ✅ Hard cap 10 MB per file, enforced before disk write
✅ UUID rename; original retained as metadata only
✅ Signed URL with expiry; non-guessable path; outside web root
✅ ClamAV integration or S3 + Lambda scanner before serving

slides.memory_hook: Trust no input from the client. Validate everything server-side. AI defaults to unsafe — boundaries must be explicit.
slides.narration: File upload security. Safe versus unsafe. AI defaults to unsafe. MIME validation — magic-byte verification server-side, not the Content-Type header. File size — hard cap before disk write. Filename — UUID rename. Storage — signed URL with expiry. Virus scanning — ClamAV or S3 plus Lambda.

narration_script.speaker: Vikram
narration_script.text: File upload security. AI's defaults are unsafe. Boundaries must be defined explicitly.

narration_script.speaker: Anjali
narration_script.text: MIME validation — do NOT trust the Content-Type header. DO perform magic-byte verification server-side using libmagic or file-type. File size — hard cap, ten megabytes per file, enforced BEFORE disk write.

narration_script.speaker: Vikram
narration_script.text: Filename storage — do NOT write the original filename to disk. DO rename to UUID and retain original as metadata. Storage location — do NOT place files in a predictable web-root path.

slides.title: The Defect AI Reliably Produces — Closed → Reopen
slides.subtitle: First-pass behaviour contrasted with FDD requirements
bullets: FDD requirement — closed issues are locked. No inline comments permitted. Reopen occurs only via a dedicated dialog requiring a reason.
AI first-pass behaviour — permits inline comments on closed issues. Permits reopening without a reason.
Cause — Closed → Reopen is one of sixteen transitions but carries a SPECIAL UI rule (dialog-only) that imprecise prompts omit.
Symptoms identified by QA — closed issues displaying new comments; reopened issues with no reason in the audit log.
slides.closing_thread: The re-prompt that resolved the defect follows.

AI first pass permits inline comments on closed issues and reopening without reason. Cause — special UI rule omitted from imprecise prompts.

slides.title: The Surgical Re-Prompt That Resolved It
slides.subtitle: Three sentences · specifies the exact files · specifies the exact remediation

hero_stat.label: remediated 4 files · 1 component, 1 dialog, 1 service, 1 test — approximately 15 minutes elapsed

bullets: Ineffective re-prompt — 'fix the Closed issue thing'. Vague; AI guesses; a turn is wasted.
Effective re-prompt (three sentences):
→ "In CommentSection.tsx, when issue.status equals 'Closed', do not render the inline comment form. Render a locked message and Reopen button instead."
→ "On Reopen button click, open ReopenDialog with a required 'reason' textarea (minimum 10 characters)."
→ "In issue.service.ts, transition to Reopened must reject if reason is missing or under 10 characters — return 400 with message."
Result — 4 files modified, 1 component plus 1 dialog plus 1 service plus 1 unit test added. Approximately 15 minutes elapsed.
slides.memory_hook: Surgical re-prompt — specify the file, specify the function or component, specify the remediation shape. Three sentences maximum.
slides.closing_thread: Next — the practice most learners omit. Commit the work.

In issue.service.ts, reject transition if reason missing or under 10 chars — return 400.

slides.title: Commit Per Validated Component — The Discipline That Preserves Engagements
slides.subtitle: The practice that should have commenced on Day 1 — remediated here
slides.opening_hook: AI generates code at machine velocity. Without Git, no rollback is possible. Without commits, no history exists.
bullets: If git init was not executed on Day 1 — execute now — cd into project folder; git init; add a .gitignore; git add .; git commit -m 'initial scaffold'.
Create a GitHub repository (private). Add as remote — git remote add origin <repository-url>. Push — git push -u origin main.
Going forward — commit per VALIDATED component. Not per AI generation. Validate first. Commit second.
Example commit messages — 'feat(auth): JWT plus bcrypt plus route guards validated'; 'fix(workflow): closed→reopen dialog reason required'.
End-of-day push — git push. GitHub now mirrors the local state. This artefact becomes your submission for review in Module 6.

list.name: Database indexes
list.desc: AI commonly omits indexes on (status, projectId), (assigneeId), (dueDate). The Lead runs EXPLAIN ANALYZE and adds missing indexes.

list.name: RLS or scoped queries
list.desc: Row-level security, or service-layer scoping by user.tenantId. Re-verify every list endpoint excludes cross-tenant data. AI defaults to permissive.

list.desc: Magic-byte MIME verification, UUID rename, signed URL, virus scan. Even when specified, audit the implementation. Read the code.

list.name: Audit log integrity

list.name: Workflow boundary tests

cards.label: Path A — primary path
cards.reveal: Create an issue → traverse Open → InProgress → InReview → Resolved → Closed. At each step, append a comment. Verify the audit log records every transition with comment.

cards.label: Path B — closed lock
cards.reveal: On the Closed issue, attempt to append an inline comment. UI must display LOCKED message plus Reopen button. No form. UI parity verified.

cards.label: Path C — reopen dialog
cards.reveal: Activate Reopen. Dialog opens. Submit empty — rejected. Submit with reason — succeeds. Verify reason appears in the audit log of the issue detail.

cards.label: Path D — prohibited API
cards.reveal: Issue curl. POST /api/issues/<id>/transition with target='Resolved' from Open. Must return 400 with 'prohibited transition' message. A 200 response indicates the server-side guard is absent.

cards.label: Path E — file upload
cards.reveal: Attach a 12 MB file — must be rejected (size constraint). Attach an .exe disguised as .pdf — must be rejected (magic-byte check). Attach a 2 MB PDF — must be accepted; verify re-download via signed URL.

slides.title: Identify the workflow prompt failures
slides.subtitle: Indicate each clause violating the five-section workflow prompt rule
slides.text: Add a status workflow with states Open InProgress and Done. Users can change status by selecting it. Allow comments. The closed status should be final but maybe people can reopen.

flaws.explanation: Only three states — the FDD specifies six. InReview, Resolved, Reopened are omitted. AI ships an incomplete state machine; the client's process is broken at launch.

flaws.phrase: Users can change status by selecting it
flaws.explanation: Who is permitted to change WHAT? No role allow-list. No matrix. AI ships permissive behaviour — Reporters may close other users' issues. RBAC is entirely absent.
Permitted how? Mandatory on status change? Resolution note required on closure? Reopen reason? None specified. The audit trail becomes flat, uninformative, and tamper-prone.
'Maybe' is not a specification. AI invents a permissive reopen — no reason field, no dialog, no guard. This is the exact defect addressed in Act 4. Repeats indefinitely until prompts become explicit.
